dedupe_keys.name: loss of 38 starlink satellites in the february 2022 geomagnetic storm

description: This case study, published by T.-W. Fang and co-authors at NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center with the SpaceX Starlink guidance team in Space Weather in November 2022, examines why Starlink lost 38 of the 49 satellites launched on 3 February 2022. A minor to moderate geomagnetic storm expanded the thermosphere, and the newly deployed satellites in very low orbit could not climb against the added drag and re-entered. Using SWPC observations, forecasts and the operational coupled Whole Atmosphere Model and Ionosphere Plasmasphere Electrodynamics (WAM-IPE) model, the authors estimated densities along the orbits: the storm raised neutral density by 50 to 125 percent at 200 to 400 km, and the Starlink team's pre-launch Monte Carlo analysis with the empirical NRLMSISE-00 model underestimated the effect. A companion study by Dang and others in the same journal traced the storms to an M1.0 flare and two coronal mass ejections. The paper is accessible online as open access under CC BY 4.0, and CIRES summarised it for the public. Caveats: orbital data come from the operator, and the analysis covers one launch. The authors call for drag-focused alerts as Solar Cycle 25 intensifies. It illustrates post-event analysis of space weather hazard exposure for satellite communication infrastructure; related records are NOAA SWPC products, DONKI and Space-Track SATCAT.
